the crack energy in the plane strain problem is a linear function of the initial stress, that the crack energy is a function of the initial stresses in the direction of the crack, that the crack energies of the two cracks are different and that the difference in the crack energies of two coplanal cracks is a function of initial stresses in the plane of the cracks.
the crack energy W depends on the initial stresses, the crack opening pressure p, the crack length a, the crack separation distance b, and the anisotropy parameters.

the plane strain problem for the determination of the crack energy in a neo-Hookean elastic anisotropic medium containing two copplanar cracks.
the problem of determining the elastic energy of two coplanalr cracks in a neo-Hookean elastic medium with anisotropic material properties and initial stresses.
the problem of determining the energy release rate of a single crack and two coplanar parallel cracks in an initially stress neo-Hookean infinite anisotropic medium.

the crack energy W increases as the initial stress increases, and that the increase in W is greater for larger initial stress and smaller crack separation distance.
